releases.body:
This release brings lilbee to more coding agents. opencode and pi install it from npm, and `lilbee launch pi` starts pi on your local models. The lilbee skill now works with or without the MCP server, and it stays current when you upgrade. You can also install lilbee with one command on macOS, Linux and Windows. Source links in chat open only files inside your document folders.

## Before you upgrade

If you install with a package manager or an executable, which is the recommended path, there is nothing to do.

If you use the npm launcher:

| Change | What to do |
|---|---|
| The npm version now follows the lilbee version, and the launcher runs exactly the lilbee release its package names | Update the npm package to move to a new lilbee release. `lilbee prepare` no longer upgrades on its own. |
| `LILBEE_CHANNEL` is removed | Remove it from your environment. Pin a version with `LILBEE_RELEASE`. |

## lilbee in more coding agents

Pull requests: #1237, #1235, #1239

The `lilbee` npm package now carries an opencode and pi plugin. It adds the lilbee MCP server and both lilbee skills.

```bash
opencode plugin add lilbee      # opencode 2.x
pi install npm:lilbee
```

`lilbee launch pi` starts or reuses `lilbee serve`, then runs pi with lilbee as its model provider and MCP server for that session. It writes nothing into pi's config, so nothing is left behind when the session ends. Add `--no-mcp` to keep lilbee as the provider only.

The usage guide has one table with the install command for each agent: Claude Code, opencode and pi.

## The lilbee skill

Pull requests: #1244, #1319

- The skill works through the lilbee MCP tools when they are connected, and through `lilbee --json` when they are not. It is about 100 lines, down from 321. Tuning and settings moved to two reference files the agent opens only when you ask.
- `lilbee launch` refreshes the skill when you upgrade lilbee. A skill folder you edited is left alone, with a message that says how to get the new version.
- `--no-mcp` still installs the skill, because the skill also covers the command line.
- The Hermes launcher asks before it writes its config, its token or the skill.

## One-line installers

Pull request: #1337

```bash
curl -fsSL https://lilbee.sh/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
irm https://lilbee.sh/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installers pick the same build as the npm launcher: the right CPU, CUDA or ROCm build for your machine. They install into a user folder with no sudo or admin rights, and add it to your PATH. Set `LILBEE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` to leave your shell startup files alone. Run the command again to upgrade. A package manager is still the recommended way to install, because it also keeps lilbee up to date.

Each release now has a `SHA256SUMS` file, and the installers refuse a download whose checksum does not match it.

The npm launcher picked the CUDA 12.4 compat build for a Linux machine without AVX2 whose driver supports only CUDA 12.1 to 12.3. That build cannot run there. The launcher now picks a build the driver can run.

## Safer source links

Pull requests: #1298, #1317

- A source that names a path outside your document folders, such as `../../etc/passwd`, an absolute path or a symlink that points out, shows as plain text with no link.
- A `file:` link inside the answer text no longer opens.
- On macOS, a source that would start a program, such as an app bundle, a `.command` file or a Finder alias, does not open.
- The opener runs off the UI thread, so a slow opener no longer freezes the chat screen.
- A symlink loop shows as plain text and no longer breaks the Sources line.

## Saved chats

Pull request: #1299

A saved turn keeps its sources as data. A resumed chat in the TUI no longer shows a turn's sources twice, and older turns show exactly as they were saved.

## Server and API

Pull requests: #1320, #1263

- A JSON request body that is not valid UTF-8 gets a 400, not a 500, in the error shape of each API.
- The OpenAPI schema lists the 40

This is a big release. lilbee now has profiles: you pick a set of settings made for your kind of documents, and `lilbee analyze` reads your files and recommends one. Answers send their sources as structured data, so every client shows the same clean list. And lilbee installs into Claude Code as a plugin with two commands.

## Before you upgrade

If you install with a package manager or an executable, which is the recommended path, there is nothing to do.

If you install with pip or build on lilbee:

| Change | What to do |
|---|---|
| `huggingface_hub` floor is now 2.4.0 | pip upgrades it. Pin 2.4.0 or later if you lock dependencies. |
| `filelock` floor is now 4.2.9 | pip upgrades it. |

## Profiles

Pull request: #1003

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A profile is a named set of ingest, OCR, chunking and retrieval settings. Pick one for code, papers, scans or notes, and lilbee shows you exactly where every setting gets its value.

### Built-in profiles

| Profile | Made for |
|---|---|
| Default | Mixed documents |
| Code repository | Source code and its docs, with OCR off |
| Research papers | Two-column papers with tables, with layout detection and table extraction |
| Scanned archive | Scanned pages, with OCR on scanned pages and layout detection |
| Notes and markdown | Markdown notes and wikis |

### Pick, compare and share

```bash
lilbee profile list
lilbee profile apply research-papers
lilbee profile show
lilbee profile diff
lilbee profile new "Mine" --from research-papers
lilbee profile export "Mine" ./mine.toml
lilbee profile import ./mine.toml --target project
```

- A profile applies to all projects. With `--target project`, it applies to the current project only.
- `lilbee profile show` lists each setting with its value and its source: the profile, your change, or the default. The TUI Profile tab, the REST API and MCP show the same source.
- `lilbee profile diff` shows your changes against the profile and which of them need an index rebuild. `apply --reindex` rebuilds when a change needs it.
- A profile file can credit its authors and name the documents it was tuned on. `lilbee profile list` and the Profile tab show both.

### Corpus analysis

`lilbee analyze` samples your documents and recommends a profile with values fitted to them. It also runs on a folder before you add it.

```bash
lilbee analyze ~/papers
lilbee analyze --apply
lilbee analyze --save "My papers"
```

The TUI, the REST API and MCP can run the same analysis and apply its result.

### Safer settings writes

- If lilbee cannot write `config.toml`, it refuses the change and names the file.
- In the TUI, a failed write shows as a message instead of a crash.
- When another lilbee process changes a setting, the running one picks up that change before its next write.

## Sources as data

Pull request: #1245

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Every source now comes with its label, its citation number and its page or line span as data. The Obsidian plugin is the first to gain: it shows each source as plain text from these fields instead of parsing lilbee's markdown, so a crawled page title can no longer render as a stray link, image or HTML in your vault.

| Field | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `label` | The name to show: a page title, a file name or a memory |
| `citation_number` | The `[n]` the model cites in the answer |
| `locator` | The span the answer read, such as `page 3` or `lines 10-20` |

- `/api/ask`, `/api/chat`, both stream endpoints, `/api/search`, MCP search and the CLI JSON output all send these fields.
- The Obsidian plugin release that follows this one reads these fields. Update lilbee first, then the plugin.
- Any other client can do the same: no regex over the Sources list.
- Chat sessions store their sources beside the answer. A restored session shows the same list as the live answer, in the TUI, the session API, MCP and the export.
- Sessions saved by an older lilbee open as before.

## Claude Code plugin

Pull request: #1236

> [!IMPORTANT]
> lilbee is now a Cl

This patch release finishes the crawl work of 0.6.90b690. You can now set a crawl login in the terminal app and in the settings, crawl logs are quieter, and Wikipedia formulas come through intact.

## Before you upgrade

If you install with a package manager or an executable, there is nothing to do.

## Crawl login in the settings

Pull request: #1177

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A crawl login is now a setting, not only a command-line option or an environment variable. The terminal app's crawl dialog also takes a login for one crawl.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `crawl_login_host` | The host the login goes to: a bare host name, with an optional port |
| `crawl_authorization` | The `Authorization` header |
| `crawl_username`, `crawl_password` | A user name and password |
| `crawl_cookie` | A `Cookie` header |

- The secret settings are write-only and masked like the API keys.
- lilbee sends a stored login only to a crawl whose addresses are all on the login host. This applies to the CLI, the terminal app, REST and MCP.
- The `LILBEE_CRAWL_*` environment variables set the same settings.
- If `crawl_login_host` is a full address such as `https://example.com`, lilbee refuses it and says so. Before, lilbee kept the value and silently sent no login.
- If an MCP `add` call does not send a stored login, the result says why.

## Quieter crawl logs

Pull request: #1178

A crawl logged one warning for each link that an exclude pattern left out: 1,101 lines in two minutes on one WordPress site. Each left-out link is now a debug line. At the end, the crawl logs one line with the count for each pattern. A start page that an exclude pattern matches still gives a warning, because the crawl does not start.

## crawlberg 1.12.3 and xberg 1.3.8

Pull request: #1175

- Wikipedia formulas keep their fractions and powers (xberg-io/html-to-markdown#940). This was a known limit of 0.6.90b690.
- A crawl sends its `Accept` headers to subdomains of the start site again.
- Text that OCR finds in a picture on a PDF page is now kept. A page with a text layer gains the text of its pictures, and a scanned page that `force_ocr_pages` leaves out keeps its text.

## Engine versions

Pull request: #1176

| Component | 0.6.90b690 | 0.6.90b691 |
|---|---|---|
| llama.cpp | memory-20261019-152820 | memory-20261019-152820 |
| llama-swap | v265 | v267 |
| gguf-parser | v0.26.4 | v0.27.0 |
| Go (engine build) | 1.27.2 | 1.27.3 |

## Other changes

- The website and the README name liter-llm, which connects lilbee to hosted and local model providers.
- The Flatpak builds beside the workspace.

## Known limits

- The model picker lists hosted models from liter-llm's catalog, which misses some names, such as `deepseek-chat`. A model name set in the config still works.


## What's Changed
* lilbee-rocm 0.6.90b690 (flake) by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1169
* lilbee 0.6.90b690 (flake) by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1171
* lilbee-compat 0.6.90b690 (flake) by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1172
* lilbee-cuda 0.6.90b690 (flake) by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1170
* Build the Flatpak beside the workspace by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1174
* Credit liter-llm on the site and in the README by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1203
* Bump llama-swap and gguf-parser by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1176
* Set the crawl login in the TUI and as settings by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1177
* Log left-out crawl links at debug and sum them up at the end by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1178
* Move crawlberg to 1.12.3 by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1175
* Say a PDF page keeps the text of its pictures by @tobocop2 in https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pull/1206

This is a very exciting release. lilbee now talks to language models through liter-llm and crawls the web with crawlberg. Both are Rust clients that replace litellm and crawl4ai. Each one ran side by side against the client it replaces.

## Before you upgrade

If you install with a package manager or an executable, which is the recommended path, there is nothing to do.

If you install with pip or build on lilbee:

| Change | What to do |
|---|---|
| The `litellm` extra is now `providers` | Install with `pip install 'lilbee[providers]'`. The `release` extra includes it. |
| litellm is removed, with no fallback | Use the `providers` extra. |

For everyone, the first re-crawl of each site re-indexes its pages once and changes their source keys. Older citations keep the old address.

## Smaller executables

The executables are about 100 to 134 MB smaller than in 0.6.90b449, the release before this one. litellm, crawl4ai and their Python dependencies are no longer in the executable.

| Executable | 0.6.90b449 | 0.6.90b690 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS arm64 | 389 MB | 289 MB | 26% smaller |
| macOS x86-64 | 424 MB | 308 MB | 27% smaller |
| Linux x86-64 | 551 MB | 417 MB | 24% smaller |
| Windows x86-64 | 417 MB | 302 MB | 28% smaller |
| Linux x86-64, CUDA 12.4 | 1,326 MB | 1,192 MB | 10% smaller |
| Linux x86-64, ROCm | 948 MB | 814 MB | 14% smaller |
| Windows x86-64, CUDA 12.4 | 743 MB | 626 MB | 16% smaller |

Sizes of the release downloads on GitHub.

## liter-llm replaces litellm

Pull request: #1065

> [!IMPORTANT]
> lilbee's model client is now one Rust package instead of 58 Python packages. It loads 40 times faster, and Ollama finally gets every setting you give it.

| | litellm 1.98.0 | liter-llm 2.4.1 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Packages the client pulls in | 58 | 1 | 57 fewer |
| Size of the client on disk | 192 MB | 38 MB | 80% smaller |
| Time to load the client | 3.2 s | 0.08 s | 40x faster |
| Packages in a `lilbee[providers]` install | 104 | 87 | 17 fewer |
| Size of a `lilbee[providers]` install | 836 MB | 728 MB | 13% smaller |

Linux x86-64, Python 3.12. Load time is the median of six runs.

| | litellm | liter-llm |
|---|---|---|
| `num_ctx`, `top_k`, `repeat_penalty` on Ollama | dropped | sent |
| A stream that stops sending tokens | hangs | ends with an error |
| A request that times out | retries | fails once |

Turning thinking off works for Ollama models, and Ollama reports real token counts. Connection errors and 429 or 5xx replies still retry. The side-by-side run covered mocked providers, live Ollama and LM Studio, and the real Gemini API. Every difference was a better result, a different request with the same answer, or sampling noise.

## crawlberg replaces crawl4ai

Pull request: #912

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Web crawls now run on crawlberg, a Rust crawler. Every default exclude pattern works, pages keep the text a browser shows, a crawl can log in to a site, and long browser crawls use less than half the memory.

### Speed

> [!NOTE]
> lilbee now respects robots.txt by default, so a crawl reads it before the first page. crawl4ai did not. The first page is slower on purpose, so the HTTP figure starts after the first page.

| | crawl4ai 0.9.2 | crawlberg 1.12.0 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP crawl, after the first page | 60.9 pages/s | 71.9 pages/s | 18% faster |
| Long browser crawl, one site | 4.6 pages/s | 5.9 pages/s | 28% faster |
| Long browser crawl, peak memory | 1,406 MB | 620 MB | 56% less |

The long crawl ran on crawlberg 1.11.1. crawl4ai saved 922 pages and crawlberg 806, because crawlberg skips the `/category/` exclude pattern that crawl4ai ignored.

A browser crawl leaves no Chrome process behind. Cancel stops it in about half a second.

### Quality

| | crawl4ai 0.9.2 | crawlberg 1.12.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Default exclude patterns that work | 32 of 68 | 68 of 68 |
| Test HTML pages that lose text a browser shows | 629 | 56 |

This release makes lilbee faster and lighter on large libraries. It also lets the engine place models on each GPU itself.

## Before you upgrade

- The first open of an older library converts it. lilbee does not embed your documents again.
- After the conversion, an older lilbee cannot read the library. To go back to an older lilbee, run `lilbee rebuild` with that version. The rebuild embeds your documents again.

## Libraries upgrade in place

Each source gets a stable id. The rest of the index points at that id, not at the file path.

| Library | First open | Later opens |
|---|---|---|
| 8.8 million sources (MS MARCO) | 34 to 37 s, 1.9 to 2.3 GiB | 1.9 s |

- The terminal app and the CLI show the progress of the conversion.
- `GET /api/health` has an `upgrade` object with the progress. MCP status shows the same progress.
- During the conversion, an HTTP request waits up to 10 s, then gets a 503. The body says that an upgrade runs. `/api/health` and the status routes still answer.

## Status on large libraries

- `lilbee status` shows the counts, the source types and the 10 newest sources.
- `lilbee status --list-sources` lists all sources, one batch at a time.
- The status screen in the terminal app loads 50 sources at a time when you scroll.
- `GET /api/documents` and MCP `list_documents` take `limit` (1 to 1000, default 50) and `offset`. The answer has `total` and `has_more`.

| Library, Apple M1 Pro | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 million sources, status read of the store | 3.8 s, 1392 MB | 0.7 s, 261 MB |
| 100,000 sources, terminal app status, first page | 10 to 56 ms, 20 to 30 MB | 5.6 ms, 11 MB |

## The engine places models on each GPU

llama-server now places chat's layers on each card. lilbee sends the space to keep free for the roles that load after chat. lilbee's own layer search is removed. The chat slots share one KV pool.

![Placing chat on a GPU: the engine reads the card's free memory after embed and rerank load, keeps space for the roles that load after chat, and places chat's layers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobocop2/lilbee/pr-assets/b449/engine-fit.png)

| Chat model, one RTX 4090 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M | 37/37 layers, 151 tok/s | 37/37 layers, 147 tok/s |
| Qwen2.5-32B Q3_K_L, 24 GB held by another process | 42/65 layers, 10.7 to 13.3 tok/s | 42/65 layers, 11.1 tok/s |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B Q6_K, 24 GB held by another process | 49/49 layers, 79 to 80 tok/s | 49/49 layers, 67 tok/s |
| Qwen2.5-32B Q3_K_L with Qwen3-Embedding-8B on the same card | 29/65 layers, 7.0 tok/s | 29/65 layers, 7.2 tok/s |

One run per cell. The Qwen3-30B row places the same layers and the same GPU memory before and after, so its lower speed does not come from the placement. A re-measure is open in #1072.

- If part of the chat model stays in system memory, lilbee logs one warning.
- An engine whose `--help` does not list the fit flags keeps the old behaviour.

## Engine changes

- lilbee gives llama-swap a request limit for each model. A busy engine queues requests.
- A shared engine stays up while a lilbee uses it. It stops after the last lilbee exits. With keep engine warm on, it stays up after the last exit; `lilbee engine stop` stops it.
- A model that does not load gives one line that tells the cause.
- On a network filesystem, the engine starts without memory mapping.
- A JSON answer becomes a tool call only when the request has tools.
- The `main_gpu` setting is removed. It had no effect. A `main_gpu` value in `config.toml` gives one warning.

## Engine versions

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| llama.cpp | memory-20261017-193536 (tobocop2/llama.cpp) |
| llama-swap | v265 |
| gguf-parser | v0.26.4 |
| Go (engine build) | 1.27.2 |

- llama.cpp comes from the fork [tobocop2/llama.cpp](https://github.com/tobocop2/llama.cpp). The fork is current upstream llama.cpp plus a `GET /memory` endpoint, which reports the memory that each model uses on each device. lilbee reads it for its memory w
